notes: The keyboard no longer hides the conversation. The chat is now built the way messaging apps build theirs — anchored to the newest message — so when the keyboard opens the messages rise with it, the latest one sits right above the message box instead of behind it, and a chat always opens on the newest message. This was checked on an Android emulator: before, the last message stayed behind the keyboard; now it rises fully into view and settles back when the keyboard closes. Connecting is faster: the app used to ask the server who you are before almost everything it did — opening a chat, coming back from the background, loading the chat list — and now reads that from the phone, so those waits are gone; a connection that dropped in the background is also noticed straight away. Signing out on another device still signs this one out too.
